transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr. Lindqvist. I wanted to come by and talk to you about your imaging results from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: About time. I've been sitting here for hours wondering why I'm still feeling short of breath. What did the CT show?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It did show a pulmonary embolism, which is why we started you on the heparin drip later last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Later last night? The scan was done yesterday morning. I know how this works. If it was on the scan, you saw it. Why did it take until midnight to start the meds?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with the initial reporting process. Things didn't go quite right with the communication between the departments.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that even mean? Issues? Was it missed? Be specific.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a bit of a complication in the workflow. The final read took longer than we would have liked.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop giving me the runaround. I was a paramedic for twelve years. I know exactly how a radiology queue works. Was the PE missed on the preliminary report? Yes or no?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just that the system can be very overwhelmed sometimes, and the preliminary notes weren't comprehensive.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you missed a clot in my lung for nearly a whole day. I'm sitting here with a potential infarct because someone didn't look at the images properly. This is negligence.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling really angry right now. It is a frustrating situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating? It's dangerous. Who is responsible for this? Who missed it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a bit of a breakdown in the coordination between the reading room and the floor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't ask for a lecture on coordination. I asked who is responsible. Did the radiologist miss it or did you not check the report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process was delayed. We are just glad we caught it and that the medication is now running.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Glad? You're glad? I've spent eighteen hours in a window of risk because of a "breakdown." I want a formal apology and I want to know exactly how many hours went by before the attending actually saw the film.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling let down by the care here. We really want to make sure you recover well.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Don't try to manage my emotions. Give me the timeline. When was the scan done and when was the treatment ordered?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The scan was early yesterday, and the orders were put in late last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Eighteen hours. Nearly an entire day of a PE going untreated. How is that acceptable?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: These things can happen in a fast-paced hospital environment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's acceptable if the patient is a statistic, not if it's a human being. What is the plan now? How do we know there aren't other things you missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on your vitals and see how you respond to the heparin.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. That's just basic care. What's the follow-up? Am I getting an echo? When is the specialist coming in?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll likely have some more tests soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Likely? When? Give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure of the exact schedule yet, but we'll be monitoring you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I want to speak to the Chief of Medicine. I want a written record of this delay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly look into who you can talk to.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now. I want the name of the radiologist who missed it and I want the attending on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give out staff names, but I can tell you that we are aware of the delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're aware of it, but you won't admit it. You haven't even said the words. You haven't said you're sorry or that the hospital messed up.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is a very stressful experience for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop saying you understand. You don't understand. You're hiding behind "workflow issues." I want a real answer. Why was I ignored for eighteen hours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, the preliminary report wasn't fully detailed, which led to the delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which means the error happened at the reading station. Now tell me what happens next to make sure I don't end up in the morgue because of another "workflow issue."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned to the monitors and see how the labs look.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Get out. Get out and find me someone who actually has the authority to tell me the truth.

H.justification: The resident shows defensive escalation under pushback, repeatedly using deflective language and failing to acknowledge the patient's specific demands.

E.justification: The resident never explicitly names the error, instead using platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'complication in the workflow'.

A.justification: No direct apology language was used, and responsibility was consistently deflected to 'the system' and 'coordination' issues.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand this is a very stressful experience') and names emotions ('angry', 'frustrated') but fails to engage with the patient's specific emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we'll keep an eye on your vitals' and 'we'll likely have some more tests soon' without timelines or specific steps.
